# Symmetric fibers: a center-only obstruction and an exact extrusion constraint

Every individual fiber here is centrally symmetric; its symmetry centers need
not form an affine graph. The affine-center theorem is already proved in
finite-center-graph-tensorization-and-budget-obstruction.md. It gives the
half-constant M/2^(n+1) when its center-graph hypothesis holds. That hypothesis
cannot simply be removed while retaining the same candidate points.

The counterexample excludes selecting among the actual symmetry centers,
even for strictly nonheavy rectangular fibers. It does NOT exclude another
actual point with depth M/2^(n+1), and does not refute OC. The structural
result records an exact actual-body constraint on center bending.

## 1. Three rational rectangular fibers

Use n=1,d=2 and continuous coordinates (x,y). Define

    B=[-1/2,1/2]^2,
    A=(1/10)B,
    s=11/20, L=279/220,
    K=sB+[0,L]e_1.

Their areas are |B|=1, |A|=1/100, and

    |K|=s(s+L)=(11/20)(20/11)=1.                     (1)

All are rectangles and hence centrally symmetric. The endpoint symmetry
centers are zero. The middle symmetry center is

    c=(L/2,0)=(279/440,0),    279/440>1/2.           (2)

Their actual Minkowski midpoint is (A+B)/2=sB subset K. Consequently

    C=conv(({-1} times A) union ({0} times K)
                            union ({1} times B))

is a full-dimensional convex body with exactly these three integer fibers.
The endpoint fibers are exact by extremality of their bases. At base zero
every endpoint interpolation lies in sB subset K, so no extra middle
points appear. Thus q=2, M=201/100, and the proposed symmetry-fiber bound
is M/4=201/400. Every fiber is strictly nonheavy, since 1<M/2=201/200.

At Y_0=(0,279/440,0), the actual ambient cap H_0={x>=279/440} captures
no endpoint volume, because their x-coordinates are at most1/2. It bisects
K and captures exactly1/2, below M/4 by1/400.

Both endpoint symmetry centers also have explicit bad closed caps. At
Y_+=(1,0,0), use H_+={x+2(z-1)>=0}. The maximum x-coordinate in K is
s/2+L=679/440<2, so K is excluded; A is excluded as well. This cap
bisects B and has mass1/2. At Y_-=(-1,0,0), use H_-={x-2(z+1)>=0}.
Again K and B are excluded, and A is bisected, giving mass1/200.
Thus EVERY symmetry-center candidate has depth strictly below M/4.
All tested caps have nonzero continuous normals and null mixed boundaries.

The center graph is nonaffine, since an affine graph through the two
zero endpoint centers would have zero middle center. This example does
satisfy OC explicitly: the larger endpoint symmetry center supplies at
least half its own area in every containing cap. The displayed isolating
cap proves its raw depth is exactly1/2, while

    (Gamma_2/2)M=67/150<1/2,
    1/2-67/150=4/75.                                  (3)

No exact global maximum relative to M/4 is asserted here.

## 2. All integer ranks and continuous dimensions at least two

For d>=2 take the continuous product with [-1/2,1/2]^(d-2), with the
usual singleton convention for d=2. Its volume is one, every resulting
fiber remains a centrally symmetric box, and the same caps have exactly
the same masses. All fibers remain full dimensional.

For n>=1 additionally take the product with [0,1]^(n-1) in integer
coordinates. The mixed source consists of 2^(n-1) binary blocks of the
three-fiber example. Its original mass and proposed target are

    M_total=2^(n-1)201/100,
    M_total/2^(n+1)=201/400.

At any selected binary vertex v, choose an affine functional ell_v that
is zero at v and strictly negative at every other binary vertex. Add a
large positive multiple of ell_v to each displayed bad-cap margin.
Boundedness of the other coordinates ensures that a finite multiplier
excludes every other block, preserving the original cap in the selected
block. This handles EVERY symmetry center with an actual closed cap.

Thus the center-only rule fails for every n>=1,d>=2. At the endpoint
center from (3), other blocks can only add to its half-volume own-fiber
guarantee. Since Gamma_d<=Gamma_2 for d>=2, the OC target after padding
is at most67/150. The separate OC-safe calibration persists.

## 3. Exact center-defect inclusion for arbitrary symmetric fibers

Let P be the finite complete integer projection of an actual convex
fiber family, and assume all its nonempty fibers are full-dimensional
centrally symmetric bodies

    K_z=c_z+L_z,       L_z=-L_z.

Fix ANY finite convex representation of an integer base p in P:

    p=sum_i lambda_i z_i,
    lambda_i>=0, sum_i lambda_i=1.

Define

    D=sum_i lambda_i L_(z_i),
    delta=sum_i lambda_i c_(z_i)-c_p.                  (4)

Actual convex compatibility says delta+D subset L_p. Reflection in zero
also gives -delta+D subset L_p. Their convex hull is exactly
D+[-delta,delta], hence

    D+[-delta,delta] subset L_p.                       (5)

Conversely (5) contains delta+D and therefore implies original convex
compatibility for this representation. Thus (5) is an EXACT equivalent
description in the symmetric class. Equivalently, for EVERY normal u,

    h_(L_p)(u)>=sum_i lambda_i h_(L_(z_i))(u)
                                  +|u.delta|.          (6)

For delta!=0 put e=delta/||delta|| and let pi_e be orthogonal projection
onto e-perpendicular. Cavalieri integration along lines parallel to e
gives

    |D+[-delta,delta]|
        =|D|+2||delta|| vol_(d-1)(pi_e D).             (7)

Each nonempty line fiber is an interval and acquires length2||delta||
over the same projection. Fubini includes the boundary fibers; their
possible zero lengths do not affect the identity. For d=1 the projection
is a point with normalized zero-dimensional measure1. Therefore

    |K_p|-|D|>=2||delta|| vol_(d-1)(pi_e D).            (8)

For delta=0 the result is just |K_p|>=|D|; no direction is required.

## 4. A uniform halfspace error with sharp coefficient

For any compact convex D and displacement delta, every ordinary closed
halfspace H satisfies

    ||(D+delta) intersect H|-|D intersect H||
         <=||delta|| vol_(d-1)(pi_e D).                (9)

Integrate along lines parallel to e. If the halfspace trace is constant
on those lines, translation changes no mass. Otherwise the trace is a
halfline, and moving an interval by ||delta|| changes its captured length
by at most ||delta||. Integration over the common projection proves (9).

Since D=-D, through-zero caps bisect D. By (8)-(9), moving the testing
center from the center of M=sum_i lambda_i K_(z_i) to c_p changes ANY
directional M-cap mass by at most

    (|K_p|-|D|)/2.                                    (10)

In particular every through-c_p continuous halfspace H satisfies

    |M intersect H|>=max(0, |D|/2-(|K_p|-|D|)/2).

The coefficient1/2 in (10) is sharp in every d>=1. Take c_p=0,
D=[-1,1] times[-1/2,1/2]^(d-1), delta=t e_1, 0<t<=1, and
L_p=D+[-delta,delta]. Its volume surplus is2t. On M=D+t e_1, the
through-c_p cap {x_1<=0} has mass1-t, losing exactly t relative to
the mass1 of a through-center cap of M. This is an actual centrally
symmetric extrusion containing the indicated translate M.

Section1 realizes its center defect by an exact extrusion too, but its
own symmetry center remains below the proposed target. Volume payment
must therefore be used while selecting or moving a center; it does not
by itself prove the symmetry-center selector.

## 5. A compatible mass-preserving deformation to affine centers

Choose any affine map a on the integer-coordinate space. For -1<=t<=1 put

    c_z(t)=a(z)+t(c_z-a(z)),
    K_z(t)=c_z(t)+L_z.

Every convex representation (4) has new center defect t delta, because
the affine terms cancel. Inclusion (5) contains D+t delta for |t|<=1.
Thus the deformed fibers satisfy EVERY integer-base convex compatibility
relation. Their convex hull has exactly those fibers at each original
integer base, and its unchanged complete integer projection introduces
no further integer bases. Every fiber volume is unchanged and each fiber
stays centrally symmetric. If the original projection spans R^n, full
continuous fibers at spanning base points give ambient interior for
every t, regardless of their translations.

At t=0 the center graph is affine and the archived theorem applies.
This is a valid deformation, not a depth-transfer theorem. No depth
monotonicity, concavity, or preservation of a maximizing center along
t is claimed.

## 6. A positive equal-endpoint-volume bridge

For an arbitrary three-fiber convex body at -1,0,1, let the endpoint
bodies A,B have the SAME volume v>0. They need not be centrally
symmetric. Let the middle K be centrally symmetric about c, with
volume k. Then the actual point (0,c) has raw depth at least

    max(k/2,v)>=(k+2v)/4.                            (11)

Use the proved dominated midpoint coupling from
accepted fact 486fe778f838d99d, f6641f09c19819a3:
there is a joint measure pi of mass v with endpoint volume marginals,
whose midpoint pushforward eta has density at most one on (A+B)/2
subset K. This follows from triangular conditional quantile transport;
the proof and its full change-of-variables details are in that source.

For any ambient cap through (0,c), if the midpoint of a coupled pair
lies in its middle trace H_0, at least one endpoint lies in the
corresponding endpoint trace: the endpoint margins average to its
midpoint margin. Integrating gives U_A+U_B>=eta(H_0). When the
continuous normal is nonzero, symmetry gives |K intersect H_0|=k/2.
Because eta<=1_K dx and eta(K)=v,

    eta(H_0)>=max(0,v-|K minus H_0|)=max(0,v-k/2).

Adding the own contribution proves max(k/2,v). A pure integer cap
contains the entire middle fiber and an endpoint, with mass k+v,
which is larger. Closed boundaries in nonzero continuous directions
are null for eta and all full-dimensional fibers. General containing
caps reduce to their parallel through-source caps. Thus all ambient
halfspaces are covered at ONE actual symmetry center.

This is a genuine all-d result for the stated equal-endpoint class.
Unequal endpoint volumes are essential in Section1. It does not
prove the half-constant for arbitrary symmetric-fiber families.

## 7. Unequal endpoints: two symmetric fibers suffice for a uniform 2/9 bound

Let A,K,B be full-dimensional convex bodies at bases -1,0,1, with
(A+B)/2 subset K and volumes0<a<=b and k>0. Suppose K and B are
centrally symmetric; A may be arbitrary. Then one of the TWO actual
points (0,c_K),(1,c_B) has raw depth strictly greater than

    (2/9)(a+k+b).                                     (12)

In particular this proves the n=1 OC target for this class in EVERY
d>=2, since Gamma_d/2<=2/9. It includes all three-symmetric-fiber
families in arbitrary positive continuous dimension, but is not an
arbitrary-fiber-count or arbitrary-integer-rank theorem.

The full unequal-endpoint coupling is proved in
candidate a972493c7a264f4e,
Section1. It supplies one measure eta, simultaneously for every direction
and threshold pair, with

    eta(R^d)=a,   eta<=(a/v_*)1_K dx,
    v_*=((a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2)^d,
    eta(H_0)<=U_A+(a/b)U_B<=U_A+U_B.                (13)

This is the actual full endpoint coupling; no selected subbody replaces
B. Briefly, the triangular conditional transport has derivative product
b/a. Its midpoint map has product Jacobian at least v_*/a by expanding
product_i(1+t_i) and applying AM-GM to each fixed-cardinality family of
terms. Repeated one-dimensional substitution gives the stated density,
and the pointwise midpoint cap implication proves the final inequality.
The source gives every regularity and substitution detail without a
smoothing assumption.

At c_K a nonvertical through-source cap has own volume k/2. Domination
in (13) gives eta(H_0)>=max(0,a-ak/(2v_*)). Pure integer caps have
volume at least k+a, which is larger than the resulting bound. Thus

    D_S(0,c_K)>=k/2+a max(0,1-k/(2v_*)).           (14)

Separately D_S(1,c_B)>=b/2. The same two points are used for every
halfspace; after comparing their two deterministic bounds, choose the
point with the larger one. AM-GM gives v_*>=sqrt(ab).

Here is a complete scalar inequality. Normalize b=1, set u=sqrt(a)
in(0,1], and continue to denote k/b by k. Twice the best certified
raw bound from (14) and b/2 is at least

    F(u,k)=max{1,k,(1-u)k+2u^2}.

For every0<=u<=1 and k>=0,

    F(u,k)/(1+u^2+k)>=4/9,                         (15)

with equality ONLY at u=1/2,k=1.

If0<=u<=1/2, the third term is at most max(1,k): check separately
k<=1 and k>=1, using2u<=1. The ratio of max(1,k) to1+u^2+k is
minimized at k=1 and equals1/(2+u^2)>=4/9. Equality has the asserted
unique parameters in this range.

Suppose1/2<u<1. The upper envelope changes from1 to the third line
at k_0=(1-2u^2)/(1-u), when this is nonnegative, and from the third
line to k at k=2u. If k_0<0, its left endpoint is k=0 instead.
On each of these intervals, an affine numerator divided by1+u^2+k
has derivative of constant sign, so it is enough to check the listed
endpoints and the limit1 at infinity. At k=2u,

    2u/(1+u)^2-4/9
       =2(2u-1)(2-u)/[9(1+u)^2]>0.

At a nonnegative k_0,

    9/4-(1+u^2+k_0)
       =(2u-1)(2u^2+3u-1)/[4(1-u)]>0.

If k_0<0, then u^2>1/2, and the ratio at k=0 is
2u^2/(1+u^2)>2/3. Finally at u=1 the envelope is max(2,k), whose
ratio to2+k has minimum1/2 at k=2. This proves (15) and the equality
classification without a lower restriction on k.

The relaxed equality point corresponds to a=b/4,k=b. At this point
a differs from b, so strict AM-GM gives v_*>sqrt(ab)=b/2 in every
finite d. Hence (14) is strictly greater than b/2. At every other
parameter point (15) is already strict. The original two-point
certificate is therefore strictly greater than (2/9)(a+k+b), proving
(12). This is a fixed positive scalar surplus for the given body, so
taking the infimum over caps does not lose strictness.

The counterexample in Section1 is consistent with (12): it refutes
the stronger1/4 center-only constant, not this2/9 guarantee. No
claim that2/9 is sharp for actual finite-dimensional bodies is made;
it is sharp only for the relaxed scalar envelope (15).

## 8. The reflected-pair scalar assembly has a strict seven-fiber gap

The coupling bound (14) can be summed at a symmetry center, but this
particular volume-only assembly is not universally sufficient. Here is
the exact scope and an actual convex-fiber certificate.

Fix an occupied base p whose full-dimensional fiber K_p is centrally
symmetric about c_p, with volume k. For every unordered reflected pair
{z,2p-z} of other occupied bases, write its two volumes as a_z<=b_z and
put

    v_z^*=((a_z^(1/d)+b_z^(1/d))/2)^d.

Different reflected pairs are disjoint. Applying (13) separately to each
pair, always at the SAME point (p,c_p), gives

    D_S(p,c_p)>= k/2+
        sum_pairs a_z max(0,1-k/(2v_z^*)).          (16)

The support of each coupling lies in K_p by actual midpoint inclusion.
A nonvertical through-source cap has own mass k/2; domination bounds
each pair's missed coupling mass by a_z k/(2v_z^*). This proves (16)
simultaneously for all nonvertical caps. A pure integer through-source
cap contains K_p and at least one endpoint of every reflected pair.
Its mass is at least k+sum_pairs a_z, so it also obeys (16). Extra,
unpaired fibers contribute nonnegative mass and are not used here.
The finite menu in question consists of these bounds at every occupied
base and the individual own-fiber half-volume bounds. It does not
include arbitrary source relocation or additional shape-sensitive
information about the couplings.

Take d=2, J any centrally symmetric planar convex body of area one and
center zero, and a nonzero P in J. For -3<=z<=3 define

    r(z)=1-|z|/4,   K_z=P+r(z)(J-P).

These are the exact integer fibers of the full convex body

    C={(z,x): -3<=z<=3, x in P+r(z)(J-P)}.

Indeed r is positive and concave, and 0 belongs to J-P; a convex
combination of two fibers lies in the fiber over the averaged base by
concavity and the nesting of dilates of J-P. Compactness and nonempty
ambient interior are immediate. Every fiber is centrally symmetric
about (1-r(z))P, a nonaffine center graph. Its area is r(z)^2, giving

    (V_-3,...,V_3)=(1/16,1/4,9/16,1,9/16,1/4,1/16),
    M=11/4.

The exact values of (16) are

    p=0:       1/2+1/16=9/16,
    p=+/-1:    9/32+1/8=13/32,
    p=+/-2:    1/8+1/32=5/32,
    p=+/-3:    1/32.

For example, at p=1 the pair(0,2) has v^*=9/16 and contributes1/8;
the pair(-1,3) has v^*=1/4 and contributes zero. At p=2 its sole
pair(1,3) has v^*=1/4 and contributes1/32. These account for every
reflected pair. Consequently the best value of this entire menu is

    9/16 < 11/18=Gamma_2 M/2,
    11/18-9/16=7/144.                              (17)

This is not a counterexample to OC or to all symmetry-center selectors.
An explicit safe point is Y=(0,P/4). The three fibers at -1,0,1 all
contain the same copy E=(3/4)J+P/4, of area9/16, and Y is its center
in the middle fiber. For any nonvertical through-Y ambient cap, the
two endpoint traces have opposite thresholds about this center.
Central symmetry therefore makes their captured E-volumes sum exactly
9/16, while the middle E contributes9/32. Pure integer caps have still
larger mass. Hence the single actual point Y has raw depth at least

    27/32 > 11/18.

The strict failure in (17) is thus precisely a limitation of the
volume-only residual-coupling assembly, even on actual symmetric fibers
with a nonaffine center graph.

## 9. Exact global depth in the center-selector counterexample

The Section1 body has an explicitly deeper point than any of its
symmetry-center candidates. In fact

    max_(y in S) D_S(y)=101/200,
    Y=(0,5/8,0) attains this value.                  (18)

This exceeds M/4=201/400 by1/400. Thus the center-only counterexample
does not exclude the existence of an unrestricted quarter-depth point.

Recall A=[-1/20,1/20]^2, B=[-1/2,1/2]^2, and

    K=[l,h] times[-H/2,H/2],
    l=-11/40, h=679/440, H=11/20.

For the upper bound, take any point (0,x,y) in the middle fiber. There
is a finite integer tilt with middle trace {X<=x}, capturing A fully
and missing B: take the coefficient alpha in -X+alpha z>=-x
sufficiently negative. This cap has raw mass

    G(x)=H(x-l)+1/100.

If x<=1/2, G(x)<=349/800<101/200. If x>1/2, the pure continuous cap
{X>=x} misses both endpoints and has mass F(x)=H(h-x). In that case
F(x)+G(x)=101/100, so their minimum is at most101/200. This covers
every middle point, independently of its y-coordinate. At either
endpoint, a finite exposing integer tilt isolates any prescribed own
cap. The maximal possible ordinary depth of that endpoint is at most
half its area, hence at most1/2. This proves the global upper bound.

For the lower bound, fix an arbitrary nonzero continuous normal
u=(u_1,u_2) and any ambient through-Y cap. Its endpoint offsets can
be arbitrary subject to averaging to u_1(5/8). The middle symmetry
center is c_K=(279/440,0), and c_K-(5/8,0)=(1/110,0). The horizontal
translation estimate (9) therefore bounds the mass change from the
through-c_K cap by H/110=1/200. Every such own cap has mass at least
99/200, and when u_1>=0 its mass is at least1/2.

We use an elementary exact endpoint credit. If there exists v with
A+v subset B and u dot v>=2u_1(5/8), pair each X in A with v-X in B.
The average of the two endpoint cap margins is nonnegative. At least
one member of every pair is captured, so endpoint mass is at least
|A|=1/100. This includes equality and all closed-boundary cases;
the continuous boundaries themselves have area zero.

If u_1<=0, choose v=0. The endpoint credit plus99/200 gives101/200.
Suppose u_1>0 and write r=|u_2|/u_1. Since

    B minus_Minkowski A=[-9/20,9/20]^2,

one can choose v with A+v subset B and u dot v=2u_1(5/8) whenever

    (9/20)(u_1+|u_2|)>=(5/4)u_1,
    equivalently r>=16/9.

For these normals the own cap contributes at least1/2 and the endpoint
credit gives at least51/100. For the remaining normals r<16/9, use
16/9<36/11. Every horizontal line of K meets the middle cap at a
threshold inside its x-interval, because

    r H/2 <= min(5/8-l,h-5/8)

holds whenever r<=36/11. Integrating the affine threshold over the
symmetric y-interval yields exactly

    |K intersect H_0|=H(h-5/8)=101/200.

This proves the lower bound for every nonvertical ambient cap. A pure
integer cap through Y captures the entire middle fiber, so it has
mass at least1>101/200. Every containing cap includes its parallel
through-Y cap. Finally {X>=5/8} captures exactly101/200, proving
attainment and (18) with no angular or source-selection omission.
